title: Tangongon abaca (NSIC Mt 03): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Tangongon abaca: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Tangongon abaca is an abaca variety for Mindanao. 18 to 21 months to harvest. See its ratings and traits. Compare it with others.
excerpt: Tangongon is a registered abaca variety, also sold or known as NSIC Mt 03. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2017 as NSIC 2017 Mt 03. It takes 18 to 21 months from planting to the first harvest.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Tangongon abaca takes 18 to 21 months from planting to the first harvest. That is 2 months faster than the average of the 3 abaca varieties with a day count, 21.5 months. Count the months from planting, and plan the harvest for a dry stretch when you can.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting. Read up on [Fusarium wilt](/diseases/fusarium-wilt).

The pests and diseases that hit abaca fields most often: [Banana aphid](/pests/banana-aphid), [Banana bunchy top](/diseases/banana-bunchy-top), [Banana weevil](/pests/banana-weevil), [Fusarium wilt](/diseases/fusarium-wilt). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
It is straight or slightly curved.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** Fiber yield listed as 1,590 to 1,700 per hectare.
**Fruit:** Strong, heavy fiber, tensile strength about 49 to 60 kgf/g m.
Poor stooler but large, heavy stalks.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: large, vigorous Mindanao abaca that tolerates drought and heavy clay, fiber strips easily. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Tangongon abaca

It is recommended for Mindanao. Abaca needs rain spread through the year and a little shade. Pick a variety by fiber yield and strength, and plant clean suckers or tissue cultured plantlets. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is NSIC Mt 03 the same as Tangongon?
items.a: Yes. NSIC Mt 03 is another name for Tangongon, registered as NSIC 2017 Mt 03. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 18 to 21 months from planting to the first harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
It is recommended for Mindanao. Ask your municipal agriculturist how it has done in your town.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Tangongon?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
